Single spacecraft 3D analysis as SOHO LASCO C2. Using the source location at N16W04, we find the front deflected NE, and without the ability to triangulate in real-time. As such, this region's eruptive history is referenced, and a latitude of N30 then fitting the longitude to E03 is used to approximate the parameters, and may vary as a result. This deflection does fit with the observed wide opening field lines in SDO AIA 193.
Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

Preliminary shock analysis with only several available GOES CCOR-1 frames. Due to the limited frames and full halo presentation, the shock width could vary, impacting speed. Current preliminary analysis of the shock is consistently around 1200 km/s, with high confidence in the latitude and longitude.

Updated 3D single spacecraft analysis using SOHO LASCO C3. STEREO A COR2 returns from a data gap at 2026-07-01T00:09Z and observes the CME material but the LE is just beyond the FOV at that time and cannot be tracked. This is enough to use COR2 to estimate the more northward latitude than preliminary analysis and estimate the half width, while no frames are officially included in the analysis.

Very faint, wide CME visible to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 only. The CME disappears half-way through the C2 field of view. The potential source for this CME is the M2.6 flare peaking at 2026-06-21T02:46Z from Active Region 14473 (S08E67) as seen in SDO/AIA 131. There is an associated failed filament eruption in SDO/AIA 304 starting around 2026-06-21T2:39Z through 2026-06-21T03:30Z. Additionally, there are moving/opening field lines visible in SDO/AIA 131 starting around 2026-06-21T02:55Z which appear to be successful in releasing from the lower corona.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on source location and best fit using SOHO LASCO C2 imagery. The CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Due to this, some uncertainty with parameters is present.

The source of this CME appears to be filament ejecta from along the Western limb in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery starting around 2026-06-21T07:15Z, possibly associated with old Active Regions 14464 and 14467 beyond the SW limb from STEREO A's point of view.

The source is an M6.8 flare from Active Region 14473 (S09E57) starting around 2026-06-21T19:25Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. An EUV wave is observed surrounding the eruption site in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195 at this time as well.

This location is in close proximity to an equatorial coronal hole to the West of the source region, and the CME may be deflected to the east as a result.

A very faint opening of field lines may be visible beyond the southwest limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery starting around 2026-06-23T08:05Z.

data.note: Loop CME seen to the east-northeast in SOHO LASCO C2, C3 and STEREO A COR2A. The CME appears to be associated with eruptive activity over the eastern limb, as evidenced by opening field lines bending from eastward to the northeast seen in SDO AIA 171 imagery starting around 2026-06-23T18:00Z. The full extent of the eruption is better visualized in GOES SUVI 284 imagery, where a faint loop seen stretching from northeast to southeast begins erupting outward off the eastern limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Fairly speculative leading edge measurement using only Sun-Earth line coronagraphs which include SOHO and GOES with no STEREO Ahead imagery, therefore, there is high uncertainty in source longitude by up to 15 degrees.

data.note: CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-23T01:26Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This CME is mostly blocked by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME is a region of dimming seen centered at approx. N40E50 beginning at approx. 2026-06-24T00:49Z as seen in SDO AIA 193 with some likely deflection towards the Northwest.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the NE by GOES CCOR-1 beginning at 2026-06-24T13:00Z. This CME is not clearly seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a downlink data gap from 2026-06-24T06:24Z to 2026-06-24T15:36Z, and is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to it being far sided from the COR2A perspective. The source of this event is a small eruption from Active Region 14475 (S09E32) beginning at approx. 2026-06-24T10:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131 and 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: Faint, thin CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2, more faintly in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely triggered by AR 14477 (S13E55), with two weak brightenings observed at S11E55 and N00E40 and an area of dimming in between centered around S01E51, all in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-06-25T23:16Z, also observed in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 171 as field line movement originating from this area.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Half width is less than 10 degrees in SOHO, appearing slightly more wide in STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and potentially to the SW in STEREO A COR2, it is difficult to resolve but a faint feature is visible in COR2A white light imagery only. No direct source is observed for this event, likely far-sided, and may be visible as weak field line movement in SDO AIA 171 around 2026-06-25T03:31Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only plane-of-sky due to the faint front. While a faint signature is observed in STEREO A COR2 white light, it is not resolvable in running difference imagery to reliably triangulate with.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The front starts slow and faint in LASCO C2, becoming more defined further into the respective fields of view. No distinct source is observed for this event, an eruption in SDO AIA 193 from AR 14470 at 2026-06-25T14:37Z was a culprit but occurs too late for the slow start time of this front.

cmeAnalyses.note: GOES CCOR-1 only plane of sky as the CME is blocked by the LASCO C3 pylon.

data.note: CME observed to the SW in STEREO A COR2, not yet visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a downlink gap and GOES CCOR-1 due to a data gap. The source is a filament eruption over the SW limb from Earth, and on-disk for STEREO A. Observed as filament ejecta over the SW limb in SDO AIA 304 starting at 2026-06-25T13:25Z and also in GOES SUVI 304. Observed on-disk brightening and field line movement in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 starting at 2026-06-25T13:25Z near former AR 14469, putting the approximate center filament location ~S15W115. Also observed as field line movement and filament ejecta in SDO AIA 131/171/193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2, and available SOHO LASCO C3 imagery at this time due to a downlink gap.
Preliminary approximation of the far sided source around W115 as viewed in STEREO A EUVI, could vary W105-W125. STEREO A COR2 only observing coronagraph at this time.

data.note: CME first seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-06-25T16:36Z. It is also seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the SW in STEREO A COR2. No independent source has been found for this CME. It is most likely outflow following CME: 2026-06-25T14:38Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement due to lack of triangulation.

data.note: Very narrow CME first seen to the E in GOES CCOR-1 starting around 2026-06-25T21:15Z. It is also seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C3. It is covered by real time data gaps in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2. The source of this CME is most likely some nearly continuous eruptive activity from AR 14478 (S06E64).

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on probable, on-disk source location.

data.note: CME first seen to the W part way into the FOV of STEREO A COR2. This CME is only seen in STEREO A COR2, and the start is covered by a real-time data gap. The start of this CME is also covered by a data gap in STEREO A EUVI. The front is only visible for three frames and is later overtaken by CME: 2026-06-25T23:48Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very speculative plane-of-sky measurement based on three frames from STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Narrow CME first seen to the NW in GOES CCOR-1 starting around 2026-06-25T21:24Z. It is mostly obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3 and is covered by real-time data gaps in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely some minor field line movement seen beyond the NW limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2026-06-25T21:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to far-sided source candidate and lack of triangulation.

data.note: Narrow CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-06-25T23:00Z. It is also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 but is not seen in STEREO A COR2. No source candidate has been found on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement due to lack of triangulation.

The front is best seen to the W in STEREO A COR2. Measurement indicates that the source of this CME is far-sided, but the start time is covered by data gaps in STEREO A EUVI.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME first seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-06-26T00:24Z. It is also seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 but is not seen in STEREO A COR2. The source is most likely some opening field lines seen beyond the limb in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-06-25T23:34Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: 3D SOHO LASCO C2/C3 analysis using approximate source of far-sided filament, with updated Solar Orbiter EUVI 304 imagery observing a likely filament eruption spanning approximately E130-E90 (centered around E110, used here). Longitude could vary slightly as a result.

data.note: CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is a farsided filament eruption centered around approximately S15W120, near former AR 14469. Observed as filament ejecta and moving field lines over the SW limb in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 starting around 2026-06-26T01:16Z. Also observed on-disk as filament ejecta, brightening, and field line movement from former AR 14469 in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 starting around 2026-06-26T01:15Z.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2, and faintly in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. No source is observed for this event, but it does closely follow and present similarly to prior CME 2026-06-26T00:24Z at E110 and CME 2026-06-26T02:24Z at E144.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 plane-of-sky due to the unseen far-sided source and no STEREO A COR2 visbility to triangulate.

data.note: Streamer blowout CME observed to the W in STEREO A COR2, and as a faint halo in SOHO LASCO C2 better observed on the northern halo edge. No distinct source for this CME is observed, and is likely far-sided. The bright west streamer in STEREO A COR2 blows out following the leading edge of this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and the faint halo signature in SOHO LASCO C2.

data.note: Narrow CME first seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2 starting around 2026-06-26T05:08Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2. There is not a definitive source candidate for this CME, but it is possibly related to some very minor field line fluctuation near the eastern footpoint of a filament centered around N27E10 beginning a couple hours prior to the CME start time best seen in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Speculative triangulated measurement based on limited imagery from STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2.

data.note: Narrow CME first seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-06-26T08:24Z. It is also seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. No definitive source candidate has been identified. It is possible that this feature could be related to some activity starting around 2026-06-26T06:10Z near AR 14478, but the timing makes this unlikely.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to lack of source candidate and lack of triangulation.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The front starts very faint in LASCO C2 and develops more clearly further into the respective coronagraphs' field-of-view. The source is faint but likely field line movement and brightening from former AR 14468 observed in STEREO A EUVI 195 at 2026-06-26T05:35Z, and subtly over the NW limb in SDO AIA 193 around ~2026-06-26T05:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and SW in STEREO A COR2. No source for this CME is observed, likely far-sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The front is quickly overlapped in STEREO A COR2 by CME 2026-06-26T15:09Z. The source is likely dimming and field line movement centered around S30W90, observed best in STEREO A EUVI 195 starting around 2026-06-26T13:35Z, with likely westward deflection caused by the nearby coronal hole east of the eruption.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME observed to the SW in STEREO A COR2, and as a partial halo to the S/W in SOHO LASCO C2. The source is far-sided from Earth, likely a newly developed active region observed ~W160 in Solar Orbiter PHI at 2026-06-26T05:39Z. This source is observed in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 starting around 2026-06-26T13:35Z as field line movement and filament ejecta on or just beyond the SW limb, which is ~W152.4 with STEREO A at W62.4. Likely associated with a GOES-equivalent M1.0 [C6,M2] flare observed in Solar Orbiter STIX peaking at 2026-06-26T14:35Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Shock triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.
Bulk triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME first seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-06-26T19:12Z. It is also seen to the SE in GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2. It is mostly missed in real time by SOHO LASCO C3 due to a gap between downlinks. There are a couple source candidates for this CME. The first is some minor field line movement near the SE limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning as early as 2026-06-26T17:48Z. The second candidate is near-continuous activity and fluctuation from AR 14478 that is best seen in SDO AIA 193 for hours prior to and following the CME start time.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulated measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME first seen to the W in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-06-26T19:34Z. It is only seen in STEREO A COR2A. The majority of the propagation is covered by a real-time data gap in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely an eruption seen near the W limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 starting as early as 2026-06-26T18:35Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to beyond-limb source candidate and lack of triangulation.

data.note: CME first seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-06-26T21:12Z. It is also seen to the S in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the SE in STEREO A COR2. The most likely source candidate for this CME is a region of southward directed dimming best seen in SDO AIA 195 starting around 2026-06-26T17:34Z centered around S30E05. There is also some field line movement likely associated with this dimming over the S limb best seen in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2026-06-26T20:06Z and in GOES SUVI 284 beginning around 2026-06-26T19:49Z. A much less likely source candidate for this CME is associated with a C2.4 class flare from AR 14475 (S09W04) that peaked at 2026-06-26T20:21Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131, but the eruption followed by some post eruptive arcades is best seen in SDO AIA 304 and SDO AIA 195.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated measurement with imagery out to 21 solar radii. High confidence in front-sided fit.
PRELIMINARY measurement based on triangulated best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 as well as on most probable source location.

data.note: Puff-like CME seen to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2, C3 and GOES CCOR-1, also seen to the south-southeast in STEREO A COR2A; the source appears to be eruptibe activity just beyond the eastern limb as evidenced by a plume of rising plasma seen best in GOES SUVI 304 imagery and also as moving magnetic field lines in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-06-27T02:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge of the CME using triangulation between SOHO/GOES and STEREO A for determination of the source longitude.

data.note: CME observed to the E only in STEREO A COR2, likely due to being directed towards the SOHO and GOES occulting disks. The source is not too clear, with the most likely candidate being field line movement and slight filament ejecta observed in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 on or near its east limb starting around 2026-06-27T13:45Z. This could also correspond to a brightening loop in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-06-27T15:33Z centered ~N05E26 between AR 14479 and AR 14478.

cmeAnalyses.note: 3D STEREO A COR2 only analysis using the approximate source longitude around E26, near STEREO A COR2's east limb. With the uncertain source and lack of triangulation, longitude may vary.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2, very faintly in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. This CME front carries some uncertainty with it as the leading edge in STEREO A COR2 overlaps with the same triangulation for CME: 2026-06-27T19:12Z, which features a front to the SE in SOHO and GOES. The source for this CME is likely far-sided, with a newly developed active region located around W170-W180 (previously located ~W150-W160 at 2026-06-26T07:09Z in Solar Orbiter PHI). It may be visible in STEREO A EUVI 195 over its west limb starting 2026-06-27T15:05Z, but this is quite early. Solar Orbiter STIX observed an estimated GOES-equivalent X1 [M6, X2] flare from this approximate area of the disk peaking at 2026-06-27T18:20Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. There is uncertainty in this analysis due to this front in STEREO A COR2 also tracking well with a separate feature in SOHO, for CME: 2026-06-27T19:12; as such it is plausible there was a farsided simultaneous eruption that overlaps in COR2 but not in C2.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 and SW in STEREO A COR2, very faintly in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. This CME front carries some uncertainty with it as the leading edge in STEREO A COR2 overlaps with the same triangulation for CME: 2026-06-26T18:53Z, which features a front to the SW in SOHO and GOES. The source for this CME is likely far-sided but not observed in any EUV imagery, and may be associated with an active region located around E140-E160 (previously located ~E150-E160 at 2026-06-26T07:09Z in Solar Orbiter PHI).

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. There is uncertainty in this analysis due to this front in STEREO A COR2 also tracking well with a separate feature in SOHO, for CME: 2026-06-27T18:53Z; as such it is plausible there was a farsided simultaneous eruption that overlaps in COR2 but not in C2.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the SW in STEREO A COR2 and very faintly to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2, following and overlapping with CMEs 2026-06-27T18:53Z and 2026-06-27T19:12Z. No distinct source for this CME is observed, likely farsided, and could be associated with an active region located around E140-E160 (previously located ~E150-E160 at 2026-06-26T07:09Z in Solar Orbiter PHI).

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2, tracking a very faint leading edge. this leading edge is in close proximity to the leading edges of CMEs 2026-06-27T18:53Z and 2026-06-27T19:12Z, but did not track to them; as such this is likely a separate event amidst those two also on the farside.

data.note: CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2, and faintly in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is filament ejecta from around the SE limb, deflecting southward after erupting, observed best in GOES SUVI 304 starting around 2026-06-27T19:14Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2 only plane of sky due to the sharp deflection and unknown farsided longitude source of deflected filament ejecta.

data.note: This CME is visible to the north/northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a filament eruption centered near N50W05 which begins to lift off, with a northeast deflection, starting around 2026-06-28T00:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 304 imagery. Dimming is also observed near the eruption site in SDO AIA 193 imagery starting around 2026-06-28T01:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

data.note: This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a far-sided filament eruption which begins to lift off around 2026-06-28T03:00Z seen beyond the northwest limb in STEREO A EUVI 304, SDO AIA 171, and GOES SUVI 171/284/304 imagery. An opening of field lines is visible over the northwest limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery at this time as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is a filament eruption visible over the southeast limb in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery which begins to lift off around 2026-06-28T04:30Z. An opening of field lines is visible over the southeast limb in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery around this time as well.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the approximate source location. A triangulated measurement was not available as this CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

data.note: This CME is visible to the north/northwest in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery for a few frames before becoming too faint/diffuse to observe. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of 90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-28T18:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This CME is not clearly seen in GOES CCOR-1 as it is blocked by the pylon, and is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to poor image quality. The source of this event is likely far sided, but faint field line movement is seen along the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-06-28T17:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using a longitude of W90 due to source from beyond the limb and lack of coronagraph imagery to triangulate.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the N by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-28T20:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This CME is not clearly seen in GOES CCOR-1 as it is blocked by the pylon, and is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2026-06-28T19:38Z. There is no clear source seen for this CME as it is likely far sided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement using a longitude of W90 due to likely far sided source and lack of coronagraph imagery to triangulate.

data.note: CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The potential source of this event may be an eruption seen around S10W85 in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery with post-eruptive arcades and dimming after a data gap in STEREO A from 2026-06-28T19:25Z to 2026-06-29T00:25Z. There is a filament eruption centered around S10W110, but the timing of the liftoff, starting around 2026-06-29T00:55Z, appears to be too late to be associated with this CME. This CME exhibits possible deflection from the source location due to its proximity to a coronal hole.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery in SWPC_CAT. This CME exhibits deflection from the potential source location, possibly due to proximity to a coronal hole.

data.note: CME seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The CME is likely obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 and is not visible. The potential source is an eruption seen in SDO AIA 193 around N15E20 as dimming starting at 2026-06-29T02:42Z. Opening field lines are also visible near the NE limb in STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT as well as the potential source location. Limited imagery was available for a measurement due to the faint leading edge.

data.note: Faint CME seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and the SSW of STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is a filament eruption centered around S35W100 as seen in STEREO A EUV 195/304 imagery starting at 2026-06-29T04:45Z. The eruption is also visible off the southwest limb in GOES SUVI 304 and SDO AIA 304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on potential source location and the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT. The leading edge is not clearly measurable in GOES CCOR-1 imagery.

data.note: CME visible to the east in GOES CCOR-1 and faintly to the west in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME is not seen in real-time in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a downlink data gap. The source is likely farsided as seen as moving field lines in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA and SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-06-29T06:57Z. An estimated M4.0 class solar flare was observed on the farside from the point of view of the Solar Orbiter/STIX, located around longitude -158, at 2026-06-29T07:29Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT. The leading edge is faint and unclear in running difference imagery, and this measurement is approximate.

data.note: CME observed to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and NW in STEREO A COR2, likely obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely in the vicinity of AR 14479 (N16W03), observed as field line brightening and movement followed by dimming in SDO AIA 193 starting as early as 2026-06-29T09:26Z spanning to approximately 2026-06-29T14:00Z, centered ~N15E05. Also observed here in STEREO A EUVI 195 starting at 2026-06-29T11:05Z. This source timing is early, but slow to evolve, so still a good candidate that aligns with triangulation. Partially overlapped by following CME 2026-06-29T17:36Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME observed to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and NW in STEREO A COR2, likely obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely in the vicinity of AR 14479 (N16W07), observed as field line brightening and movement followed by dimming in SDO AIA 171/193 starting as early around 2026-06-29T17:18Z, centered ~N13W05. Also observed here in STEREO A EUVI 195 starting at 2026-06-29T17:25Z. Partially overlapped by prior CME 2026-06-29T16:38Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the W in STEREO A COR2, and faintly to the W in SOHO LASCO C2. The source is likely an eruption in the vicinity of former AR 14471, located approximately N17W140 at this time. Likely observed in STEREO A EUVI 195 at 2026-06-29T17:15Z as a brief dimming and field line movement near the NW limb from STEREO A.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2, and the very faint front in SOHO LASCO C2 better observed in running difference imagery.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, likely obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 and not in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting at 2026-06-29T19:38Z. The source is associated with an M1.4 class flare from AR 14479 peaking at 2026-06-29T21:40Z observed in SDO AIA 131. Also observed in SDO AIA 171/193 as brightening, field line movement, and slight dimming following the flare. The CME front appears deflected slightly NE from the source region.

cmeAnalyses.note: Single spacecraft 3D analysis as SOHO LASCO C2. Using the source location at N16W04, we find the front deflected NE, and without the ability to triangulate in real-time. As such, this region's eruptive history is referenced, and a latitude of N30 then fitting the longitude to E03 is used to approximate the parameters, and may vary as a result. This deflection does fit with the observed wide opening field lines in SDO AIA 193.

data.note: This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely an eruption from Active Region 14479 (N16W15) starting around 2026-06-30T13:30Z which exhibits northern deflection as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery. Dimming is observed northeast of the eruption site in SDO AIA 193 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: Full halo CME currently observed only in GOES CCOR-1 and somewhat blocked by its pylon. Not yet observed in other coronagraphs due to a SOHO LASCO DSN gap between 2026-06-30T20:15Z to 2026-06-30T23:45Z, and STEREO A data gap starting at 2026-06-30T19:23Z. The source is associated with an X1.1 flare (N17W18) observed in SDO AIA 131 from AR 14479 (N16W22), peaking at 2026-06-30T20:50Z. Also observed as a NE-deflected EUV wave and wide swath of dimming in SDO AIA 193/211 centered around N20W05, brightening/flare ribbons along a channel to the NE of the region in SDO AIA 131/171/193/211/304, and a post-eruptive brightening starting around 2026-06-30T21:46Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary shock analysis with only several available GOES CCOR-1 frames. Due to the limited frames and full halo presentation, the shock width could vary, impacting speed. Current preliminary analysis of the shock is consistently around 1200 km/s, with high confidence in the latitude and longitude.

Updated 3D single spacecraft analysis using SOHO LASCO C3. STEREO A COR2 returns from a data gap at 2026-07-01T00:09Z and observes the CME material but the LE is just beyond the FOV at that time and cannot be tracked. This is enough to use COR2 to estimate the more northward latitude than preliminary analysis and estimate the half width, while no frames are officially included in the analysis.

Preliminary bulk anaylsis with only several available GOES CCOR-1 frames. Due to the limited frames and full halo presentation, the CME width could vary, impacting speed. Current preliminary analysis of the bulk is consistently around 900-1000 km/s, with high confidence in the latitude and longitude.

data.note: Feature first seen to the ENE in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-07-01T00:38Z. It is also possibly visible in SOHO LASCO C2 but not traceably so. There is no separate source candidate for this front; it is most likely outflow following CME: 2026-06-30T21:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement with STEREO A COR2 due to lack of triangulation and lack of source candidate.

data.note: Feature first seen to the ENE in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-07-01T03:23Z. It is also possibly visible in SOHO LASCO C2 but not traceably so. There is no separate source candidate for this front; it is most likely outflow following CME: 2026-06-30T21:45Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement with STEREO A COR2 due to lack of triangulation and lack of source candidate.

data.note: CME first seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-07-01T03:48Z. It is also seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME is most likely opening field lines on or slightly beyond the E limb best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-07-01T03:38Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen due to lack of triangulation and source on/beyond E limb.

data.note: Very faint front to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-07-01T12:12Z for a couple of frames before the start of a gap between downlink periods. The start time is somewhat ambiguous due to the faintness and overlap with an earlier feature to the N. This CME is also seen to the NNW in GOES CCOR-1. It is covered by real-time data gaps in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely associated with an M1.0 class flare from AR 14479 (N13W33) that peaked at 2026-07-01T11:25Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131. The accompanying eruption including dimming, opening field lines, and an EUV wave is best seen in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Speculative, PRELIMINARY measurement based on early frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 as well as on visible source location.

data.note: CME first seen to the NE by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-07-01T16:23Z. This CME is not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a downlink data gap from 2026-07-01T12:48Z to 2026-07-01T18:47Z, and is not clearly seen in GOES CCOR-1. The source of this event is a long duration M2.6 flare from Active Region 14479 (N16W32) which peaked at 2026-07-01T14:54Z as seen in SDO AIA 131. Dimming, field line opening and post eruptive arcades are also visible in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME first seen to the East by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-07-01T17:23Z. This CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a downlink data gap from 2026-07-01T12:48Z to 2026-07-01T18:47Z, and is not clearly seen in GOES CCOR-1. There is not clear source seen for this event, and lack of SOHO and GOES imagery makes  triangulation difficult.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A plane-of-sky using a longitude of E27 due to lack of clear source and no GOES or SOHO imagery to triangulate source.

data.note: CME first seen to the North by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-07-02T00:06Z, following a data gap which ended at 2026-07-01T23:54Z. This CME is also seen to the North in SOHO LASCO C3 and to the Northeast in STEREO A COR2 following a data gap which ended at 2026-07-02T00:08Z. This CME is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source of this event is an M3.5 flare from Active Region 14479 (N15W32) which peaked at 2026-07-01T19:43Z as seen in SDO AIA 131. Field line opening and post eruptive arcades are also visible in SDO AIA 171, 193 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-07-01T21:24Z. This fronts fades before exiting the field of view in C2, and is therefore not visible in SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 or GOES CCOR-1. The source of this event is an M2.0 from Active Region 14480 (S14W38) which peaked at 2026-07-01T19:35Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, along with post eruptive arcades seen in SDO AIA 171 and 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2.

data.note: CME associated with M4.2-class solar flare in Active Region 14799 located near N17W39; the CME is comprised of a separate brighter bulk seen to the north in SOHO LASCO C2 and seen to the east-northeast in STEREO A COR2; the fainter shock is extremely wide relative to the bulk and is seen faintly all the way from due west to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2 and from the north to the southeast in STEREO A COR2A. The eruption is characterized by a circular shock front seen in EUV imagery, particularly in GOES SUVI 284 imagery as there was an ongoing SDO AIA outage at the time.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge/bulk measurement using only SOHO/STEREO A as the CME is obscured by the pylon in GOES. Strong eastward deflection along the Earth-Sun line with high confidence as this is visually confirmed in EUV imagery.
Shock front incorporating very wide shock feature seen to the west in LASCO and to the southeast in STEREO A COR2A simultaneously. To do so requires a width >50 degrees.

data.note: CME observed to the W in STEREO A COR2 and E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. No source is observed directly for this CME, likely on the eastern far-side from Earth. Partially overlaps with CME: 2026-07-02T09:38Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME observed to the SW in STEREO A COR2 and SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. No source is observed directly for this CME, likely on the eastern far-side from Earth. Partially overlaps with CME: 2026-07-02T08:53Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Minor, narrow CME seen to the north-northwest in SOHO LASCO C2 and to the northeast in STEREO A COR2A which could be associated with a minor eruption on the Earth-facing disk seen near the vicinity of Active Region 14479 (N17W47) or farther to the east seen near 2026-07-02T11:20Z best in GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement of the CME using SOHO C2, a few frames of SOHO C3, and STEREO A COR2A.

data.note: Faint CME to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, briefly in C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may be moving/opening field lines visible along the NE limb in SDO/AIA 193 and 171 starting around 2026-07-02T22:00Z. This feature overlaps the CME: 2026-07-03T02:00Z in STEREO A COR2 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There may be some uncertainty with parameters due to overlapping features from the perspective of STEREO A COR2.

data.note: This slow CME is visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery and NE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. It is obscured by the control arm in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There is no clear source for this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: Very narrow CME visible to the E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. It is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is no clear source for this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky parameters based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. The CME is slightly more narrow than the measurement constraint of 10 degrees half-width.

data.note: Narrow CME visible to the W in STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is no clear source for this CME.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky parameters based on best fit in STEREO A COR2 imagery using a longitude of 153 degrees.

data.note: CME first seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-07-03T14:24Z. This CME fades before reaching the edge of the FOV of SOHO LASCO C2 and is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a real-time gap between downlink periods. The most likely source candidate is a wide loop and opening field lines seen beyond the W limb in GOES SUVI 284 beginning around 2026-07-03T14:17Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement based on running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2.

data.note: CME first seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-07-03T18:36Z. It is also seen to the NW in GOES CCOR-1 and to the NNE in STEREO A COR2. Only the first couple of frames in SOHO LASCO C2 are seen in real time due to a data gap between downlink periods. This CME is associated with an M6.7 class flare from AR 14479 (N15W58) that peaked at 2026-07-03T18:11Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131. A large EUV wave and wide opening field lines are also seen in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: PRELIMINARY measurement based on best fit among GOES CCOR-1, STEREO A COR2, and early frames of SOHO LASCO C2 as well as on visible source location.
PRELIMINARY SHOCK measurement based only on source location and fit in GOES CCOR-1. Real-time data gaps in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 cover the majority of the propagation of the CME.

data.note: Narrow CME seen to the east in SOHO LASCO C2, faintly in GOES CCOR-1, and not well at all in STEREO A due to a data gap. The CME is likely associated with the M6.3-class solar flare from Active Region 14478 occurring near S10W53 with a narrow jet of plasma being seen erupting near the active region best in SDO AIA 131 and a large loop structure leaving the southwest limb in GOES SUVI 284 near 2026-07-03T19:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement of the CME along the Sun-Earth line using only SOHO and GOES imagery and knowledge of the suspected source location, as the CME is not seen well in STEREO A imagery.

data.note: CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is partially obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3 imagery and is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME is likely farsided, with moving field lines visible beyond the NW limb in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA, SDO AIA 193, and GOES SUVI 284 imagery. Between a data gap from 2026-07-04T13:45Z to 2026-07-04T17:15Z, a filament on the west limb as seen from STEREO A EUV imagery (approximately N20W155) can be seen lifting off. The exact longitude of the filament is unclear as both footpoints are not clearly visible in EUV imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate potential source location using SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: CME seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is visible to the NW in STEREO A COR2 imagery after a data gap from 2026-07-04T19:53Z to 2026-07-05T00:09Z. The source location is likely farsided and not clearly visible in EUV imagery. One potential source may be a filament eruption seen erupting beyond the limb to the north in GOES SUVI 304 imagery around 2026-07-04T16:01Z. Another potential source candidate is opening field lines seen beyond the NE limb in GOES SUVI 284 and SDO AIA 171 starting at 2026-07-04T16:25Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT. Only one frame of STEREO A COR2 imagery was available for a measurement.

Plane of sky measurement using GOES CCOR-1 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT. The corresponding leading edge is not clearly discernible in STEREO A COR2 imagery for a farsided source candidate in order to triangulate this CME in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: CME seen faintly to the NE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME is not clearly visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is not clearly seen in available EUV imagery and is likely farsided.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane of sky measurement using STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: CME visible to the SW in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There is a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time. There is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery from 2026-07-04T19:53Z to 2026-07-05T00:09Z, but the CME is not clearly visible in available imagery. The likely source is an M1.5 flare from Active Region 14478 (S06W35) starting at 2026-07-04T19:23Z as seen in SDO AIA 131 imagery. Moving field lines and an ejecta of material is best seen in SDO AIA 193. The flare is also visible in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on source location using GOES CCOR-1 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: CME visible to the east in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is not seen in real-time in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery due to data gaps. The source is an X1.3 flare peaking at 2026-07-04T20:41Z from Active Region 14482 (S10E85) with an associated EUV wave and opening field lines as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary measurement based on source location using GOES CCOR-1 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

data.note: Simultaneous flaring is also observed from Active Region 14480 (S14W38) peaking around 2026-07-01T19:35Z.
Simultaneous flaring from Active Region 14479 (N19W47) and Active Region 14478 (S06W34)
Previously attributed to AR 14479 (N15W77), which appears to have a simultaneous flare starting slightly earlier as seen in SDO AIA 131 imagery.
